I'd like to take this on.

**Root cause analysis:**

1. **Race condition**: In `app.tsx`, `onMount` calls `local.model.set()` which calls `isModelValid()` — but at mount time, `sync.data.provider` is still empty (the async bootstrap hasn't resolved yet), so every model fails validation.

2. **Priority override**: Even if validation passes, the `createEffect` in `local.tsx` that watches `agent.current()` immediately overwrites the CLI model with the agent's configured model, since agent model is checked before the fallback chain that includes `args.model`.

**Proposed fix:**
- Track the CLI-specified model (`args.model`) as a reactive override in `local.tsx` with highest priority in `currentModel`
- Remove the eager `model.set()` from `app.tsx`'s `onMount` — let the reactive memo handle it once providers load
- Skip agent model auto-set when a CLI override is active

## Additional report: Windows 11 without any proxy — same error

**Environment**

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 Pro |
| opencode | 1.4.11 |
| Node | v22.22.2 |
| npm | 10.9.7 |
| Proxy | None — `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` not set, no system proxy |

**Symptom**

Every startup reports:

```
Failed to install plugin opencode-mem@2.13.0: NpmInstallFailedError
Failed to install plugin oh-my-openagent@3.17.4: NpmInstallFailedError
```

**This bug is not proxy-specific.** It reproduces on Windows with no proxy configured at all.

**Root cause narrowed down**

Through direct testing:

- Running `@npmcli/arborist` `loadVirtual()` against the same cache directory under **Node.js v22**: **succeeds** — `edgesOut` is populated, reify is correctly skipped
- Same call inside **1.4.11's embedded Bun runtime**: `loadVirtual()` throws (silently swallowed by `.catch(() => {})`), falls through to `reify()`, which then fails and raises `NpmInstallFailedError`

The root cause is **Bun runtime incompatibility with `@npmcli/arborist`'s `loadVirtual()`**, not proxy handling.

**Regression confirmed**

- `opencode-ai@1.3.17` (uses `bun add` subprocess): works fine
- `opencode-ai@1.4.11` (uses embedded arborist): fails on every startup

**Workaround**

Downgrade to 1.3.17, install plugins with explicit versions (`opencode plugin opencode-mem@2.13.0 --global`), then upgrade back to 1.4.11. The warning banners still appear on startup but plugins may still load depending on timing — not a reliable fix.

Hope this helps narrow down the Bun-side compatibility issue.

There is now a related PR for one confirmed branch of the `/sessions` visibility problem: #23276 https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/23276

That PR addresses the child-session dilution root cause described in #16270: the TUI dialog was requesting a mixed root+child session list, hitting the default limit, and only filtering root sessions client-side, so recent child sessions could crowd recent root sessions out of the picker.

I would not assume it resolves every report in this issue, though. Some comments here point at a different directory / project-scoping path after repo renames or path changes, so this PR is intended to cover the confirmed mixed-list / limit / root-filtering case rather than the whole issue family.

I opened PR #23276 to address the child-session dilution path discussed here: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/23276

It fixes the same confirmed root cause (mixed root+child session list getting limited before root filtering), but I scoped the change to `dialog-session-list.tsx` instead of changing the global bootstrap in `sync.tsx`.

Reason for the narrower patch: after tracing current `dev`, `sync.data.session` is also used by TUI session-parent / session-child navigation, so changing the shared bootstrap list to roots-only would affect a wider surface area. This PR keeps child-session data available for those flows while making `Switch Session` request root sessions directly for both the default list and search.

The repro I used locally matched the pattern in this issue: the missing root session was rank 4 among root sessions but rank 152 among all sessions because 148 newer child sessions came first.

Yes, it's exactly it. It's because the ripgrep WASM code is executed on the main thread in Bun which blocks the entire JS runtime, even if the interfaces at js level are designed to be async. When that's happening, even an inspector debugger cannot pause the excution. What it is doing is scanning your entire workspace's files to provide searching functionalities. It is triggered by `File.Service.init() -> rg.files()`. On Windows it's worse as Windows has heavier filesystem driver stack/antivirus. The JS runtime cannot be unblocked until your entire workspace is scanned.
Meanwhile, it is also a bad architectural choice in terms of security. In the past with a standalone rg.exe I can simply exclude/setting 'performance' mode for it specifically in antivirus to get high fs perf without whitelisting the entire opencode[-cli].exe. rg.exe does pure file reading and is very hard to exploit. opencode on the other hand, is a scripting host and can do much more. Now... it's just bad since if you want perf you have to broaden the attack surface. You lose the safety from process isolation.

Thanks for keeping this PR alive through the rebases. Dropping a production-infra use case in case it helps prioritization.

## Setup

I run OpenCode locally on **Apple Silicon (M5 Max, MLX-based backend, no cloud)** for an SRE workflow on a Kubernetes prod platform.

- **5 domain-scoped subagents:** k8s ops, cost, observability, incident response, gitlab ops
- **~10 active MCP servers:** Kubernetes, GitLab, PagerDuty, two Grafana instances (staging + prod), AWS Cost Management, Playwright, Obsidian, Context7, Kagi, Git

## MCP bloat hits local inference harder than cloud

A 50-80k token manifest is **4-8% of a 1M-context cloud model but 20-30% of the ~256k ceiling** on self-hostable coding models (Qwen3.5/3.6, GLM-4.5-Air).

It's also a perf problem, not just a budget one. LLM decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound: every generated token reloads model weights + KV cache from memory, and the KV cache grows linearly with context.

| Hardware            | Memory bandwidth |
| ------------------- | ---------------- |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM     | 3.35 TB/s        |
| NVIDIA H200         | 4.8 TB/s         |
| Apple M5 Max 40-core| 614 GB/s         |

That **5-8× gap** shows up directly in decode tokens/sec, and it gets worse as context grows. Prefix caching helps prefill, not decode — a bloated manifest taxes every output token of every turn.

## I already mitigate this aggressively, and it's not enough

My `opencode.json` has a top-level deny block for all MCPs, then each agent (including the primary) re-enables only what its role needs. The primary carries only general-purpose tools; every domain MCP routes through a subagent.

It works, but it has structural limits:

- **Static by design** — mid-session I can't reach a denied MCP without pre-routing through a subagent
- **Maintenance-heavy** — every new MCP = touch global deny + 5 agent allowlists
- **Creates subagents for token budget, not role boundaries** — my `gitlab-ops` subagent exists partly because the GitLab MCP (120+ tools) is too heavy to carry anywhere else, not because GitLab is conceptually its own role

## External proxies (mcp-lazy, lazy-mcp, lazy-tool) don't solve this

They collapse every tool call onto a single `execute_tool`, which breaks permission granularity. OpenCode matches rules on tool names:

```jsonc
"terraform apply *": "ask",
"git push *": "ask",
"pagerduty_manage_incidents": "ask",        // writes
"pagerduty_get_incident": "allow",           // reads — same server, different policy
"pagerduty_list_incidents": "allow",
"grafana_alerting_manage_rules": /* distinct between staging and prod instances */,
"kubernetes_kubectl_get": "allow",           // read
"kubernetes*": "ask"                         // catches writes, deletes, rollouts
```

A proxy flattens all of this onto one name. You either `allow` (and a PagerDuty acknowledgment slips through) or `ask` (and every Grafana read prompts). Neither works for prod.

## This PR is the right shape

Loaded tools keep their original names, so existing permission rules keep matching unchanged. It's **additive** to per-agent scoping, not a replacement: static scoping handles role isolation, lazy-load handles tool-ecosystem scale.

Commit 357301991624ae6c361350c1c1aca222268a6d5d dynamically imports `prettier`, `prettier/plugins/babel`, and `prettier/plugins/estree` in `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/generate.ts` (lines 32-34), but none are declared in any `package.json`.

In the Nix sandbox, `bun build` fails with:

```
error: Could not resolve: "prettier". Maybe you need to "bun install"?
error: Could not resolve: "prettier/plugins/babel". Maybe you need to "bun install"?
error: Could not resolve: "prettier/plugins/estree". Maybe you need to "bun install"?
```

Same class of issue as #22867 (missing `glob` dep). Fix: add `prettier` to `packages/opencode/package.json` dependencies.

**Workaround**: revert the commit by patching `generate.ts` to use `JSON.stringify(specs, null, 2)` instead of the prettier formatting.
The PR needs a `bun install` to regenerate the lockfile after adding `prettier` to `package.json`, otherwise the Nix `node_modules` hash will still be stale.
